exact_natural_reconstruction: For every real normed vector space E, function f:E->EReal, subset V of E, and real lam, assume SourceProper(f), convexity of V, V subset effectiveDomain(f), lam>=0, and the displayed strong convexity inequality on V for every real a strictly between 0 and 1. For every p in V and continuous real-linear functional g on E satisfying f(p)+g(z-p)<=f(z) in EReal for every z in V, and for every q in V, the real inequality toReal(f(p))+g(q-p)+(lam/2)*norm(q-p)^2<=toReal(f(q)) is asserted.
binders_and_hypotheses: E : Type* is implicit and universe-polymorphic. NormedAddCommGroup E and NormedSpace Real E are typeclass binders, making E a real normed vector space; completeness and finite dimension are not assumed.
f : E -> EReal is extended-real-valued; V : Set E is arbitrary subject to the listed hypotheses; lam : Real satisfies hlam : 0 <= lam.

hV : Convex Real V means every real convex combination of points of V lies in V. No openness, closedness, boundedness, compactness, or interior assumption appears.

hdom : V subset effectiveDomain f requires every member of V to lie in a named imported set. Its definition is absent from the allowed text; the precise finiteness guarantee cannot be verified from the name alone.

hstrong universally quantifies x:E with x in V, y:E with y in V, and a:Real with 0<a and a<1. It asserts f(a*x+(1-a)*y) <= a*f(x)+(1-a)*f(y)-coerce((lam/2)*a*(1-a)*norm(x-y)^2), interpreted in EReal with scalar multiplication in the argument and real-to-EReal coercions in the value expression.
p:E and hp:p in V specify the base point; g:E ->L[Real] Real is an already supplied continuous real-linear functional, not an arbitrary nonlinear map or a vector gradient.
hsupport universally quantifies z:E with z in V and assumes f(p)+coerce(g(z-p))<=f(z) in EReal. This is support on V only, with no assertion for points outside V.
q:E and hq:q in V specify an arbitrary comparison point. All named ordinary binders after E are explicit; no existential conclusion occurs.

finiteness_and_conversion.known_from_standard_semantics: EReal includes positive and negative infinity. EReal.toReal maps finite real coercions to their underlying real values and maps either infinity to zero. Consequently toReal is not generally an order-preserving inverse on arbitrary EReal inputs.
finiteness_and_conversion.header_only_limit: SourceProper and effectiveDomain are custom imported identifiers whose definitions are not displayed. This header alone does not establish exactly which endpoints they exclude, or the existential clause in SourceProper. Under that intended but unverified expansion, the assertion is the usual quadratic improvement of a given affine support: f(q)>=f(p)+g(q-p)+(lam/2)*norm(q-p)^2, now wholly real-valued on V.

constants_and_orientation: The strong-convexity correction is exactly (lam/2)*a*(1-a)*norm(x-y)^2 and is subtracted on the right of an upper bound for f at the convex combination.
The conclusion adds exactly (lam/2)*norm(q-p)^2 to the given affine support. There is no extra factor of 2, no asymptotic constant, and no dependence on a in the conclusion.
The support and conclusion both use g(q-p), not g(p-q). Although norm(q-p)=norm(p-q), the linear term's sign matters.

a is quantified only over the open unit interval, not its endpoints; lam may equal zero. All displayed numeric operations before coercion are real, except the outer hstrong and hsupport inequalities and arithmetic in EReal.
claim_boundaries: Given support is strengthened; existence of any supporting functional is not asserted. The theorem cannot alone produce a g at a chosen point.
No minimizer, attained infimum, uniqueness of minimizer, optimizer existence, coercivity conclusion, or global bound outside V is stated.
If an admissible instance has g=0, the conclusion conditionally gives quadratic growth from p on V, but the header does not establish that such a support exists at any p.
There is no algorithm, iterate, regret, convergence rate, sample complexity, or performance guarantee in the conclusion.
No proof BODY is present; neither proof acceptance, kernel validation, nor source-faithfulness is inferred.
vacuity_and_degenerate_cases: hp and hq rule out empty V in an actual supplied instance; if V is empty, there are no admissible p/q binders and the theorem application is vacuous.
If no g satisfies hsupport at p, the conditional theorem gives no instance there. Existence of support is a substantive outside obligation.
At q=p, linearity gives g(0)=0 and the norm term vanishes; the conclusion is reflexive even without interpreting f(p) as finite.

For singleton V, every admissible q equals p and the conclusion has no nontrivial growth content. lam=0 is permitted and yields the unstrengthened real support inequality when finiteness is justified.
The open interval for a is nonempty (for example a=1/2), so its quantifier is not vacuous for lack of interpolation coefficients.

Infinity-related vacuity cannot be ruled out merely from the names SourceProper/effectiveDomain. Under standard finiteness definitions it is excluded on V; the allowed text does not independently certify that expansion.
